questions.stem: The locus of points that are a fixed distance from a single point is a:
questions.explanation: All points at a fixed distance from a single point form a circle with that point as the centre.

questions.stem: The locus of points equidistant from two fixed points $A$ and $B$ is:
questions.explanation: The set of all points equidistant from $A$ and $B$ is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment $AB$.

questions.stem: The locus of points equidistant from two intersecting straight lines is:
questions.explanation: Points equidistant from two intersecting lines lie on the angle bisectors of the angles formed by the lines.

questions.stem: The locus of points at a fixed distance $d$ from a straight line is:

options.text: Two parallel lines, one on each side, at distance $d$
A single line parallel to it

questions.explanation: Points at a fixed distance from a line form two parallel lines, one on each side of the original line.

questions.stem: A goat is tied to a post by a rope of length $5$ m. The locus of the boundary the goat can reach is:
questions.explanation: The goat can move in any direction up to $5$ m from the post, tracing a circle of radius $5$ m.

questions.stem: To find the region closer to point $A$ than to point $B$, you should construct:

options.text: The perpendicular bisector of $AB$ and shade the side nearer $A$

questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisector of $AB$ divides the plane into two regions. The region on $A$'s side contains all points closer to $A$.

questions.stem: A point must be less than $4$ cm from $P$ AND less than $3$ cm from $Q$. The locus of valid positions is:

options.text: The area between two concentric circles

questions.explanation: The point must be inside a circle of radius $4$ cm centred on $P$ AND inside a circle of radius $3$ cm centred on $Q$. The valid region is the intersection of these two circles.
